subject: Svc account & licensing clarifications for Private/VPC pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Martin <alice.martin@riversidehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@riversidehealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Svc account & licensing clarifications for Private/VPC pilot

Hi all — looping everyone so we can lock the open questions Riverside raised for the Private/VPC pilot. Attached: riverside-sow.pdf and our current license matrix (redwood-license-matrix.xlsx). High-level asks from Riverside: shared service account model, cross-account KMS, and quick confirmation on licensing unit (per-GPU vs. per-seat).

Questions we need to answer for the pilot decision:
- Service account model: can we support a single shared service account for their org, or do we require a customer-managed dedicated service account per environment for auditability?
- KMS/BYOK: can we support cross-account key access so Riverside can keep keys in their KMS? Any product or packaging blockers?
- Licensing counting: their procurement needs a simple number. Does our Private/on-prem license count by dedicated GPU (or vCPU/host) or by concurrent tokens/throughput?
- Timeline impacts: procurement says 6–8 week lead if licensing changes are required.

Kimberly/soojin/karthik — can you each call out whether these are product/legal blockers, and a rough estimate of engineering + procurement steps needed? I'm trying to produce a short answer pack for Riverside's legal/procurement team by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Sr. Manager, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Martin <alice.martin@riversidehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Svc account & licensing clarifications for Private/VPC pilot

Jonas — quick notes from product/security perspective:

1) Service account model: recommended pattern is a customer-managed, per-environment service principal (preferred) to ensure clean audit trails and least privilege. Shared org-level accounts are possible but increase audit/rotation complexity and are not recommended for regulated healthcare customers. If procurement insists on shared SA, we can ship a hardened pattern but it requires an exception and additional monitoring (7–10 days to formalize runbook).

2) KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments today, but cross-account key access (Riverside KMS in their cloud account referencing Redwood-managed resources) is a partial gap — we need a short integration to permit cross-project/role key policies. I estimate ~2 weeks of infra eng work to validate and harden with our KMS integration patterns.

3) Licensing: our standard Private license is capacity-based (dedicated GPU/instance tiers). We can provide a simplified per-GPU SKU for procurement, but billing/legal needs to sign off; that is a commercial packaging decision, not a technical blocker.

I'll attach an internal runbook stub separately. Tagging Soojin/Karthik for resource/time confirmation.

-Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Martin <alice.martin@riversidehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Svc account & licensing clarifications for Private/VPC pilot

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Service account model: recommended pattern is a customer-managed, per-environment service principal (preferred)...

Thanks — a couple of pragmatic details from infra/ops:
- Packaging/ops work: to support the per-environment customer-managed principal cleanly we need to produce an onboarding script and validation checks (IAM policy linting, rotation verification). I estimate 2 engineer-weeks to produce the artifacts + 1 week for QA and runbook updates.
- Exception lane: if Riverside must use a shared account for org reasons, we'll accept an exception but require a compensating controls checklist (centralized audit forwarding, shorter key rotation, additional log retention). That exception process is ~5 business days to evaluate + implement controls.
- Resource ask: to hit the 6-week procurement window we should start procurement/commercial conversation now and reserve a small pilot slot with infra engineering for the two-week integration. Otherwise timeline slips to 8–10 weeks.

Action items I propose:
1) Kimberly/Karthik: confirm commercial packaging option (per-GPU SKU) today so procurement has numbers.
2) Jonas: share a one-page SOW addendum for the service-account approach (I can include the runbook language).
3) Riverside: confirm whether their procurement team needs shared SA or can accept per-environment principals.

I'll follow up with an internal JIRA and link to the pilot folder.

— Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@riversidehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@riversidehealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Svc account & licensing clarifications for Private/VPC pilot

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround and the details from Kim and Soojin. A few clarifications from our side:

- Licensing: our procurement team prefers a fixed number (the per-GPU SKU you mentioned would work best). Please send the per-GPU SKU and an example SOW line for capacity so we can route to finance.
- Service account: our security team is strongly preferring a shared org-level service account for easier rotation and central credential management across teams. They will need a compensating controls checklist (audit forwarding + shorter rotation cadence). Is the exception lane documented and acceptable for SOC2 purposes?
- KMS/BYOK: we can provide cross-account key access, but require a short technical validation. We are happy to run that in our sandbox account next week.
- Evidence: procurement asked for SOC2 report and a short list of required attestations for the pilot (data flows, log retention, key custody). Can you provide these artifacts or point us to the right link?

Procurement timeline: we will start internal approvals tomorrow; if we have per-GPU SKU + SOW addendum + compensating controls checklist by Friday, we can keep the ~6 week target. Otherwise our legal will push to the next quarterly cycle.

Appreciate the team coordinating — look forward to the SOW addendum.

Regards,
Alice Martin
Director of Cloud Security | Riverside Health
alice.martin@riversidehealth.com
